title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction Bank 1 Sensor 1
shortDescription: Heater on bank 1 sensor 1 O2 reports a malfunction fault.
fullDescription:
The PCM monitors the heater current/voltage on the bank 1 sensor 1 oxygen sensor. A malfunction condition prevents the sensor from reaching operating temperature, so closed-loop fueling is delayed and emissions rise.

The heater is the most failure-prone part of the sensor and usually fails together with the cell.
safetyImpact: Increased emissions and possible fuel-trim drift; not unsafe to drive.

fixSteps.title: Pull live data
fixSteps.instruction: Watch heater status and sensor voltage from a cold start.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse and power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify B+ on the heater feed with the key on.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Compare with the spec for that sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if heater is open
fixSteps.instruction: Use anti-seize sparingly on the threads.

faq.a: Yes briefly, but expect higher fuel use until repaired.
No - heater faults are an automatic emissions failure.

title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit
shortDescription: Turbo wastegate/bypass A control circuit fault.
fullDescription:
The PCM commands the turbocharger bypass valve to manage boost pressure. A control-circuit fault prevents proper boost regulation and can cause overboost or underboost conditions.

Persistent overboost may damage the turbo or intake.
safetyImpact: Possible turbo damage if boost runs uncontrolled.

fixSteps.title: Read boost data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare commanded vs actual boost.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Resistance and 12 V actuation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect lines and actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracks and stuck linkage.

fixSteps.title: Replace bypass valve
fixSteps.instruction: Use new clamps and gaskets.

faq.a: Briefly - reduced power protects the turbo.
Vacuum lines and the solenoid tie-pieces dry-rot.

title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Bypass valve A signal stuck low.
fullDescription:
The PCM detects the turbo bypass valve A control signal pulled below the calibrated threshold. The valve cannot relieve boost reliably.

Driving with sustained overboost will eventually crack the turbo or intercooler piping.
safetyImpact: Risk of overboost - reduce load if power becomes erratic.

fixSteps.title: Check harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for shorts and pinches near the turbo.

fixSteps.title: Measure circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Probe with key on and engine running.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Resistance vs spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid or repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Pin-to-pin repair preferred over splice.

faq.a: Usually no - it goes into limp mode.
Yes - inspect heat shields.

title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit High
shortDescription: Bypass valve A signal stuck high.
fullDescription:
The PCM detects the turbo bypass valve control signal stuck above the calibrated threshold. Boost regulation is compromised.

Diagnose with the same method as P0034 - shorts to power instead of ground.
safetyImpact: Risk of underboost - reduced performance until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Check if the signal goes to expected level.

fixSteps.title: Trace to PCM
fixSteps.instruction: Look for melted or chafed sections.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Match part number exactly.

fixSteps.title: Reflash if PCM fault
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer-only operation.

faq.a: It is the actuator side, not the boost sensor.
Yes briefly with limp protection active.

title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 / Bank 2 Sensor 1
shortDescription: Front O2 sensors appear swapped between banks.
fullDescription:
The PCM compares pre-cat sensors and finds the response patterns swapped between bank 1 and bank 2. Usually the harness was crossed during a recent repair.

Double-check that the sensors were not installed on the wrong banks.
safetyImpact: Fuel trim runs cross-banked - increased emissions.

fixSteps.title: Verify harness routing
fixSteps.instruction: Trace each connector back to the PCM.

fixSteps.title: Swap connectors if installed wrong
fixSteps.instruction: Re-route to correct bank.

fixSteps.title: Clear and retest
fixSteps.instruction: Drive cycle to confirm.

faq.a: Check banks first - this is the usual cause.
Only after a full drive cycle.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction Bank 1 Sensor 2
shortDescription: Bank 1 sensor 2 O2 signal shows a malfunction condition.
fullDescription:
The PCM tracks the oxygen sensor signal on bank 1 sensor 2. A malfunction reading indicates the sensor cannot report exhaust oxygen accurately, so fuel trim and catalyst monitoring lose reference.

Ignoring the fault risks driving rich/lean and damaging the catalyst.
safetyImpact: Possible catalyst damage if a rich condition is left unrepaired.
symptoms: Long-term fuel trim out of range

fixSteps.title: Graph sensor voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Check sweep between 0.1 V and 0.9 V at 2,500 RPM.

fixSteps.title: Check for exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect manifold, donuts, and pipes ahead of the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Test wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle and back-probe for opens or shorts to ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Torque to spec and clear codes.

faq.a: Not while the readiness monitor is incomplete.
Rear sensor faults are sometimes catalyst-related - confirm with data first.

fixSteps.title: Graph sensor voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Check sweep between 0.1 V and 0.9 V at 2,500 RPM.

fixSteps.title: Check for exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect manifold, donuts, and pipes ahead of the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Test wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle and back-probe for opens or shorts to ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Torque to spec and clear codes.

faq.a: Not while the readiness monitor is incomplete.
Rear sensor faults are sometimes catalyst-related - confirm with data first.
